incumbent.text: Wire-first differential reproduction then footer validation: construct a raw chunked request whose chunk-data footer is a bare line feed followed by a next-chunk size whose leading hex digit is swallowed by a two-byte discard; parse it with the staged parser and with a strict CRLF-requiring reference dechunker; compare body and trailing bytes; then add chunk-footer validation and rerun the differential and full suite.

hint: A local Python HTTP/1.1 parser now accumulates the two bytes after each chunk-data block and rejects any footer other than CRLF; the existing suite passes. Before the repair, a bare-LF footer plus a next size line whose leading digit was swallowed shifted the body boundary and left a complete request as trailing data. Open questions are whether another footer byte class or next-size shape still produces an accepted divergence, whether every split point behaves like whole-stream parsing, and whether valid chunked traffic changes. Build a differential matrix against a strict reference and a valid-corpus equivalence run.
